_comment: What may be stored in a handle field, stated once (#899).
CaptionBlocks.isHandleShaped. Two separate implementations in two
languages decide the same question on the two sides of the bridge, and a
rule applied on one side only is how the reported defect happened: the app
put 'DPR Dance' into tag_handles as a handle to mention, the model wrote
'@DPR Dance' into a caption bound for Instagram, and the Python check then
read that as the handle '@dpr', which belongs to somebody else.
The rule, after a leading @ or a pasted profile URL is stripped by
bare_username: not empty, every character in [A-Za-z0-9._], and not ending
in a dot. A dot is legal inside a handle (@safa.wav) but never ends one,
because the trailing punctuation of a sentence looks exactly like that.
SHAPE ONLY. Whether a value is a SENTINEL ('unknown', 'n/a', recorded when
a lookup found nothing) is a different question with a different answer,
and folding the two into one predicate would leave one word naming two
units (L118). 'unknown' is listed below as WELL SHAPED for exactly that

cases.why: the handle the reported caption should have carried
the @ is stripped before the shape is read
surrounding whitespace is trimmed, not content
a pasted profile link is a handle somebody can act on
a dot inside a handle is legal
underscores are legal
Instagram is case insensitive but the case is not an error
digits are legal, including first
a sentinel is well SHAPED; that it is a sentinel is a separate question
the reported defect: a company's display name typed into the handle field
any space at all, whatever the case
two accounts inside a sentence, stored in the org book today
prose, stored in the org book today
a person's name, with a comma and a trailing dot
a dot never ends a handle, because a full stop looks the same
Instagram has no hyphens in usernames
nothing is not a handle
whitespace alone is not a handle
the sigil with no name behind it
every leading sigil is stripped, leaving nothing
a link to Instagram itself names no account
a character Instagram does not allow
accented letters are outside the allowed set
